title: How does your phone know where you are?

lines.text: How can a tiny smartphone in your pocket pinpoint your exact location down to a single foot?
lines.caps: How does your phone *pinpoint | your exact | *location?

lines.text: It doesn't rely on just one sensor; it combines three invisible global systems simultaneously.
First, a built-in GPS chip listens to atomic clocks ticking aboard thirty-one satellites in deep orbit.
By calculating the nanosecond delays from four different satellites, it calculates your coordinates using trilateration.
When you step indoors where satellite signals fade, your phone scans surrounding Wi-Fi routers and cell towers.
lines.caps: Indoors, it scans *Wi-Fi | routers and cell | *towers

lines.text: It cross-references their signal strength against massive geographic databases to find your hallway.
lines.caps: Maps signal strength to *find | your exact | *room!

lines.text: You are constantly surrounded by an invisible matrix of navigation signals.
lines.caps: An invisible *grid of signals | follows you *everywhere!
